description:
Arabic font for Holy Quran
A high quality OpenType Font for Holy Quran

Pakistan Data Management Services is pleased to announce the release of an OpenType Font for writing Holy Quran text based on Unicode standard. The font features high quality glyphs and has support for all aeraabs/mark placements at proper places. All waqfs (special symbols) used for identifying different pauses in reading are also provided. ‘PDMS Saleem Quran Font’ provides advanced Arabic typography - close to calligraphy while retaining the beauty and legibility of Quran Majeed Arabic text.

This font is developed according to rules used in Quranic calligraphy in Pakistan, following the style of Yameen Dehlvi, who is one of the finest Quran calligraphers of Pakistan. Guidance and calligraphy of basic glyphs for the font has been provided by Mr. Mohammed Saleem. He is a student of Mohammed Iqbal Saeed and Yameen Dehlvi. Mohammed Saleem is also inspired by work of Shafiq uz Zaman (master calligrapher for Masjid Nabbawi) and frequently consults him for guidance.

This font enables desktop and internet publishing of Holy Quran using existing software supporting OTF specifications, e.g. Microsoft Word, Microsoft Publisher, Internet Explorer, etc. ‘PDMS Saleem Quran Font’ is freely downloadable from www.pakdata.com/ArabicFont.

We are confident that ‘PDMS Saleem Quran Font’ will appeal to all Arabic users, especially designers and publishers who will no longer be bound by the technological limitations of old Quran printing methods.

About PDMS: Based in Karachi, Pakistan, PDMS is developing Urdu Software products since 1986. The nationally acclaimed ‘Nastaleeq Nizami’ – Urdu Desktop Publishing software has boosted tremendously the use of computers in Pakistan by making them write beautifully in Nastaleeq script of Urdu language. More products include Urdu Computer Nizam, Ruqqa-UrduEmail, Urdu 98, Urdu Mahir, PDMS Jauhar, Quran Majeed CD. PDMS has also developed fonts for the regional languages like Sindhi and Pushto besides designing a number of Nastaleeq and Naskh fonts. PDMS is also constantly engaged in developing Internet website and portals and has designed a number of Urdu portals including UrduSeek.com, UrduNews.net, CityIslam.com. The area in which PDMS has technical expertise makes it a unique venture in Pakistan.

interpretation_notes: Font inventory is discovered at runtime from the selected font folder; add or remove font files and rerun to refresh the report.
Font family/style metadata describes the font file, not the orthography of text rendered using it.
Unicode cmap counts direct character mappings, not internal glyphs reached through OpenType substitutions.
GSUB/GPOS feature tags indicate feature availability, not quality of shaping in every browser.
Orthography, riwayah, script tradition, typography, encoding model and page layout are separate assessment dimensions.
Uthmani, Imla'i and IndoPak require source/edition evidence or comparison with a same-passage reference text.
Recitation transmission and regional script tradition require source metadata or a reference; character heuristics are not proof.
Typeface labels are inferred from font names/embedded metadata only; actual visual style needs rendered visual inspection.
A fixed Mushaf page layout requires a Mushaf ID or page and line position metadata; it cannot be inferred from a paragraph alone.
QPC code_v1/code_v2 glyph sequences are separate from ordinary Unicode text fields.
